correctness.rationale: Proposition 2.9 gives equality iff all unit-multiple p-adic digit sums agree and the factorial-product residues agree mod p. I independently replayed the complete exact-integer enumeration for all fourteen odd primes below 50; the exceptional primes and every p=37 orbit/order class matched the record. The source independently confirms the p=11 f=3 exception.
correctness.risk: The theorem is finite in p and fixed at extension degree three.

value.rationale: The converse problem is central to the cited primary work. A complete low-characteristic cubic census is a natural structural test of the new criterion, and the p=37 order-28/order-42 classes go beyond the source's displayed pure example.

final_claim: For \(q=p^3\) with odd prime \(p<50\), non-Frobenius Gauss-sum equalities occur exactly for \(p=11,23,37\); \(p=37\) has exactly five nontrivial equality classes, with the order-14, order-42 and order-28 orbit data listed in the record.
limitations: Only odd primes below 50 and extension degree three are classified.
